top.title: 2027 Willie McCovey Memorial Community Prospect List No. 12
top.description: PHOENIX, AZ - JUNE 24: Carson Bolemon #18 poses for a photo during the 2026 Draft Combine at Arizona Grand Resort Phoenix on Wednesday, June 24, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. (Photo by Aryanna Frank/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images We’re a quarter of the way through the 2027 Willie McCovey Memorial Community Prospect List! Our goal is to rank the top 44 prospects in the San Francisco Giants organization, and we’ve officially hit the 25% mark! Rounding out the first quarter is one of the many new players to the system who is on the list: left-handed pitcher Carson Bolemon, who makes his CPL debut as the No. 11 prospect in the system. The Giants drafted Bolemon with the 29th pick in July’s draft out of Southside Christian School in South Carolina. While he’s a little old for a prep player (he’ll turn 20 in April), he’s extremely experienced, as he not only starred in high school (where he threw a 19-strikeout no-hitter in the state championship game), but was also the ace of the 18-and-under Team USA squad that won the World Cup in 2025. Depending on how you like to view things, it’s either good or bad news that Bolemon was available to the Giants at No. 29, since he entered the season as the consensus top pitcher in the draft. Seen through an optimistic lens, the Giants were able to capitalize on a mildly-down year and get the pre-season top-ranked pitcher … as well as the post-season top-ranked pitcher, Jackson Flora. Seen through a more pessimistic lens, the Giants drafted a player who has already started moving downwards, as he was the ninth pitcher off the board in July, after being projected to be the first pitcher off the board a year ago. Bolemon, who is a well-built 6’4, and who famously didn’t give up a single earned run his junior year, has a fastball that’s been a little inconsistent in terms of velocity, but that has good movement that should allow it to play against righties and lefties alike. He has a very intriguing curveball, while also throwing a changeup and a sweeper, and scouts have raved about his makeup. The Giants were able to draft Bolemon because they acquired the competitive balance-round pick from the Cleveland Guardians in the Patrick Bailey trade, and ultimately those two will forever be linked. That trade will remain something of a “TBD” until we learn how good Bolemon can be, and we’re still many years away from that. Until then, we can look forward to seeing the youngster on the mound in 2027 for his professional debut, as he didn’t pitch (other than in unofficial games) post-draft. It will be interesting to see whether the Giants have Bolemon begin the year in the Arizona Complex League, or if they get him out at the start of the season by sending him to Low-A San Jose. Now let’s add to the list! As a reminder, voting takes place in the comment section. top.title: Bayelsa boat mishap death toll rises to 32, AIG visits scene
top.description: …Urges enforcement of life jacket, passenger capacity regulations By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of Zone 16, Regina Udoette, has visited Ayama-Ijaw waterside in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State following the boat mishap that claimed 32 lives. Udoette, who was accompanied by the Bayelsa State Commissioner of Police, Saka Ajao Adewale, visited the area on Monday to interact with marine transport workers and the Red Cross rescue team and receive updates on the ongoing search and recovery operation. During the visit, reports from the rescue site indicated that additional bodies had been recovered, raising the death toll from 29 to 32. The AIG commiserated with the Bayelsa State Government and residents over the tragedy, while commending President Bola Tinubu for his response and expression of sympathy following the incident. She expressed concern over alleged violations of maritime safety regulations, particularly the overloading of the vessel and failure to comply with life jacket requirements. According to her, the boat reportedly conveyed more than 500 passengers despite having a carrying capacity of 200. Udoette urged the state Ministry of Transport and marine unions to strengthen enforcement of safety regulations, particularly compulsory life jacket use and compliance with approved passenger limits. She also called for strict enforcement against operators who flout safety rules, stressing that passengers must take personal responsibility for their safety. Speaking with journalists, the AIG said she visited the waterside on behalf of the Inspector-General of Police to sympathise with the victims’ families and assess the situation. “I am here with my management team and the Bayelsa CP on behalf of the Inspector General of Police to sympathise with the people that died in the incident. I register our condolences and wish the injured quick recovery. “Besides, the maritime personnel told us of the refusal of passengers to obey safety rules, and the boat captain loaded over 500 persons for a boat with a 200-person capacity. That was a suicide mission and a disaster waiting to happen,” she said. Describing the deaths as avoidable, Udoette urged passengers and marine transport operators to comply with established safety regulations. “Some of these deaths are avoidable deaths. Many of the passengers refuse to obey safety rules. My Bible tells me obedience is better than sacrifice. There are rules and regulations on life jackets and overloading, but they refused. “For the living, this is a big lesson to everyone that wants to use a boat for their journey. They should listen to the rules. People should use common sense. This disaster is avoidable,” she added. top.title: BYU has never won a Maui Invitational championship. How can this year’s Cougars change that?
top.description: BYU players prepare to take the court against Ohio State on Nov. 2, 2026, at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City. | BYU Photo LAHAINA, Hawaii — The Lahaina Civic Center gymnasium is packed with history. Banners hang from its rafters commemorating past Maui Invitational champions, with Duke, North Carolina and Kansas dominating the count. Walls of the arena are dedicated to former Maui standouts and tournament MVPs, such as Kemba Walker, Adam Morrison, Bobby Hurley and Penny Hardaway. Nowhere to be found in the historic gym, however, is a lasting trace of BYU, despite the Cougars having participated in the Maui Invitational there four times before. In fact, as BYU makes its fifth-ever Maui appearance this week, the Cougars are now tied with San Diego State for the second-most times playing in the event without capturing a championship there. Only Memphis has made more trips to Maui (six) without ever hoisting the Wayne Duke trophy, which is presented to the lone unbeaten team after three days of hoops. Additionally, BYU has never produced an invitational MVP, and only one former Cougar — Tyler Haws in 2014 — has landed on the All-Tournament team. Given the current state of both November multi-team events and college basketball as a whole, perhaps 2026 will be the last time BYU graces the Civic Center hardwood in Lahaina and drains shots on the arena’s famous “soft rims.” It’s a shame that one of the sport’s most unique and prestigious early-season traditions is viewed as “on life support” and facing “an uncertain future.” The Protect College Sports Act could easily receive increased support from every political side if it included provisions to save the Maui Invitational — but that’s a thought for another day. If this week truly is the Cougars’ last dance in Maui, it’s their last chance to be crowned champions of the event. And it may be the best such chance they’ve ever had to do so. BYU (No. 25 in KenPom) opens its Maui slate Monday against Washington (No. 88), then will face either Ole Miss (No. 27) or Clemson (No. 75) on Tuesday. Two wins would put the Cougars in Wednesday’s title game, where many fans and pundits anticipate them to meet fellow Big 12 foe Arizona, assuming the Wildcats can survive their bracket of Colorado State, Providence and VCU. Not since 1992 has BYU reached the Maui championship game. The Cougars will likely be favored on both Monday and Tuesday, and in a situation with three games in three days, anything can happen in that third game — even toppling Arizona, if need be. “A lot of it’s going to come down to just toughness,” BYU head coach Kevin Young said of the invitational’s rapid-fire format. “I think our guys possess a lot of that.” BYU’s first time in Maui, 1992, saw the Cougars finish as runners-up, beating No. 9 Oklahoma and then Penny Hardaway-led Memphis before falling to Grant Hill, Bobby Hurley and No. 1 Duke in the championship. top.title: Josh Jacobs not expected to play vs Rams
top.description: The Los Angeles Rams could be catching a break against the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night. Green Bay is not expecting running back Josh Jacobs to play as he continues recovering from surgery to repair a fractured right ring finger. His expected absence could further complicate an already struggling Packers rushing attack and give the Rams’ defense another reason to anticipate a pass-heavy offensive approach. Josh Jacobs, with his surgically repaired right ring finger heavily protected, is giving it a go even though coach Matt LaFleur said he didn’t think it was very likely that Jacobs could play on Wednesday. Jacobs would need to convince them he could hold onto the football for… pic.twitter.com/LYcXBBV50p — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) November 21, 2026 Jacobs suffered the injury during Green Bay’s Week 9 victory over the New England Patriots and underwent surgery on November 13. Although he has returned to individual work, head coach Matt LaFleur indicated that Jacobs remains unlikely to suit up against Los Angeles. He will need to demonstrate that he can properly handle the football before returning to game action. It has been an incredibly up-and-down season for Jacobs. He missed the first six games while on the Commissioner’s Exempt List following off-field legal issues before returning in Week 7. Unfortunately, his return has not gone as planned. Across three appearances, Jacobs has recorded just 80 rushing yards on 36 carries, averaging a career-low 2.2 yards per attempt. Green Bay has struggled to establish consistency on the ground throughout the season. Through its first eight games, the Packers averaged just 60.6 rushing yards per game, one of the worst marks in the NFL. Even with Jacobs sidelined, the backfield has struggled to provide a dependable alternative. Without Jacobs, the Rams can enter Wednesday’s matchup with a clearer expectation of what Green Bay wants to do offensively. While Kaleb Johnson and the other available running backs will still get opportunities, Los Angeles can focus more attention on slowing down the passing game. That doesn’t mean the Packers will abandon the run entirely, but the Rams should have fewer reasons to fear a consistent ground attack. With the opportunity to make Green Bay one-dimensional, Los Angeles’ pass rush and secondary could play a significant role in determining the outcome.

top.title: Syracuse men’s basketball: fans don’t have to pretend all wins are good ones
top.description: Nov 21, 2026; Syracuse, New York, USA; Syracuse Orange head coach Gerry McNamara reacts during the second half against the Lafayette Leopards at the JMA Wireless Dome. Mandatory Credit: Rich Barnes-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After watching the Syracuse Orange struggle with Cornell on Wednesday, I assumed that Saturday’s game would bring out a focused, energetic squad. That didn’t happen and after having to pull out all the stops to win 84-81 over a Lafayette team that had lost by 36 to Butler and 28 to St. Bonaventure, Gerry McNamara was asked a question about the margin of victory in the wins this week. “I don’t worry. I’ll let other people worry about that nonsense, bullshit, I don’t care. Win a game you know. That’s how I grew up…..I’m not going to worry about margin of victory, all that. I know the next game I play I’m going to coach to win again. So I don’t worry about al the other stuff because at the end of the day you’re still going to have those opponents to play anyway so if you beat them, the margin of victory doesn’t, just win the game you’re playing in front of you. So my focus is on can we continue to get better.” McNamara ended the answer by talking about shooting and offense, but is that the issue? Can we talk about Syracuse’s defense giving up 80+ points to two teams this week? What about the fact that Cornell and Lafayette went 24-54 from 3 in the two games? Unfortunately for anyone who wants to espouse “Just win baby”, it’s not the case in today’s college basketball. Syracuse built their schedule around the NET formula and margin of victory against teams ranked 200th and 303rd in this morning’s KenPom is a factor. Winning 20 or 21 games might not be enough for an invite when the ACC is not off to a strong start. Right now Syracuse sits 81st in KenPom. Last year’s sub-500 team finished the year ranked 87th and the lowest ranked NCAA at-large team was Missouri who was 54th. Yes, it’s early. Yes, you have to win the games, but you cannot pretend that this shouldn’t be a concern….because it is. He went on to talk about not having juice, but why wait until it’s 20+ minutes in the game to make an adjustment to the press? This is still a young staff and they sure don’t seem to have a grasp on what they want this team to be this season. If you’re heading into desperation mode against Lafayette, even with two starters injured, that’s a big warning sign. This was a November game that almost turned into a unfathomable loss and it wasn’t the time to lecture anyone about playing to win the game. I’m sensititve to the fact that Gerry’s dealing with a lot right now- on and off the court. I’m worried that the pressure he’s putting on himself to get this program back is too much, but you can’t get this agitated over a legitimate question. He didn’t mention ISIS , but there were a lot of Shafer vibes coming out of this one….let’s hope the Albany post-game talk stays out of “cutting people’s heads off” talk.

nigeria.title: Bayelsa boat mishap death toll rises to 32, AIG visits scene
nigeria.description: …Urges enforcement of life jacket, passenger capacity regulations By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of Zone 16, Regina Udoette, has visited Ayama-Ijaw waterside in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State following the boat mishap that claimed 32 lives. Udoette, who was accompanied by the Bayelsa State Commissioner of Police, Saka Ajao Adewale, visited the area on Monday to interact with marine transport workers and the Red Cross rescue team and receive updates on the ongoing search and recovery operation. During the visit, reports from the rescue site indicated that additional bodies had been recovered, raising the death toll from 29 to 32. The AIG commiserated with the Bayelsa State Government and residents over the tragedy, while commending President Bola Tinubu for his response and expression of sympathy following the incident. She expressed concern over alleged violations of maritime safety regulations, particularly the overloading of the vessel and failure to comply with life jacket requirements. According to her, the boat reportedly conveyed more than 500 passengers despite having a carrying capacity of 200. Udoette urged the state Ministry of Transport and marine unions to strengthen enforcement of safety regulations, particularly compulsory life jacket use and compliance with approved passenger limits. She also called for strict enforcement against operators who flout safety rules, stressing that passengers must take personal responsibility for their safety. Speaking with journalists, the AIG said she visited the waterside on behalf of the Inspector-General of Police to sympathise with the victims’ families and assess the situation. “I am here with my management team and the Bayelsa CP on behalf of the Inspector General of Police to sympathise with the people that died in the incident. I register our condolences and wish the injured quick recovery. “Besides, the maritime personnel told us of the refusal of passengers to obey safety rules, and the boat captain loaded over 500 persons for a boat with a 200-person capacity. That was a suicide mission and a disaster waiting to happen,” she said. Describing the deaths as avoidable, Udoette urged passengers and marine transport operators to comply with established safety regulations. “Some of these deaths are avoidable deaths. Many of the passengers refuse to obey safety rules. My Bible tells me obedience is better than sacrifice. There are rules and regulations on life jackets and overloading, but they refused. “For the living, this is a big lesson to everyone that wants to use a boat for their journey. They should listen to the rules. People should use common sense. This disaster is avoidable,” she added. nigeria.title: Tinubu, Sanwo-Olu court Igbo community ahead of 2027 polls
nigeria.description: …Urge national cohesion, economic inclusion By Olasunkanmi Akoni President Bola Tinubu and Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, have urged Nigerians to rise above ethnic and regional divisions, emphasising the need for national cohesion, mutual understanding and inclusive economic development. The leaders made the call on Monday at the Ndigbo Lagos State Town Hall, organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiative (NNDDI) at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly the National Arts Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos. The engagement, attended by Igbo community leaders, business stakeholders and government officials, provided an opportunity to strengthen relations between the Igbo community and the Lagos and Federal Governments ahead of the 2027 general elections. Addressing participants, Tinubu urged Nigerians to embrace a shared national identity, irrespective of their ethnic, religious or regional backgrounds, saying the country’s development depended on the collective contributions of all citizens. He also stressed the importance of creating broad-based economic opportunities to enable Nigerians to contribute meaningfully to nation-building. “We must see ourselves as one people with a shared future. “Nigeria must rise above its divisions, because our true development depends on the active participation and commitment of every single citizen, regardless of background,” the President said. Earlier, Sanwo-Olu commended Tinubu for attending the gathering, describing his presence as an affirmation of the important role played by the Igbo community in the socioeconomic development of Lagos State. He acknowledged the contributions of Igbo political leaders, entrepreneurs, business associates and other stakeholders to the growth of the state. “The President’s presence here today is a significant gesture of recognition for Ndigbo and their rightful place in Lagos. “We deeply value the enduring contributions and longstanding partnerships of the political leaders, business associates, and stakeholders who continue to build this state alongside us,” the governor said. Reflecting on Nigeria’s democratic journey, particularly the political developments of 1999, 2003 and 2007, Sanwo-Olu also paid tribute to past and present leaders whose contributions helped shape the country’s political evolution. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Solo Bitcoin Miner Wins $191,000 Block Reward With Just 11 TH/s A solo miner running about 11 terahashes per second has mined Bitcoin block 977,057, collecting a reward of 3.1287 BTC, or about $191,000, on a machine that makes up roughly one-millionth of a percent of the network. The block was found through the solo service at CKpool on Sunday, Nov. 22, at about 7:54 a.m. ET. The reward is the 3.125 BTC subsidy plus about 0.0037 BTC in transaction fees, and it was worth roughly $191,000 at bitcoin’s price when the block landed. How the solo block played out The block holds 584 transactions. Its coinbase transaction pays 3.0661 BTC to a single address and 0.0626 BTC, about 2% of the reward, to a second output. That split matches the service’s 2% fee, which means the miner’s take is a little over $186,000. Con Kolivas, the developer behind CKpool, congratulated the miner on X, whose address he abbreviated as bc1q~zy9j. It matches the end of the address that received the payout. Kolivas called it the 323rd block found on the service and “yet another lucky one.” He said the miner had only about 11.1 TH/s of hashrate on a 3.47 TH worker. “A miner of this size has about a one in 1650 chance of solving a block in a year,” Kolivas wrote. The block was tagged to Solo CK on the mempool.space block explorer, and its coinbase carries the pool’s signature. CKpool describes itself as a service that lets miners go after full solo blocks without running their own node, since you cannot mine directly to a Bitcoin Core node. A recent run of solo wins Solo CK has found five blocks since Nov. 6, according to the explorer’s pool page . The most recent before this one was block 976,642 on Nov. 19, followed by blocks on Nov. 11, Nov. 7 and Nov. 6. Each paid between 3.13 and 3.15 BTC. Earlier this year, a different solo miner won block 943,411 on the same service on April 2, for about 3.139 BTC. In October, a FutureBit Apollo solo miner found block 973,262 and earned 3.154 BTC. Those wins are the exception. Most of the network’s hashrate sits in large pools and industrial operations that split rewards across many miners, which is how they smooth out the luck. A single small machine can run for years without finding anything, and a lucky block can show up on day one. Miners on the service get nothing unless they find a block, and then they keep the full reward minus the 2% fee. business.title: Cross River Bank Launches Its First Bitcoin-Backed Loans With LendingUSA
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Cross River Bank Launches Its First Bitcoin-Backed Loans With LendingUSA Cross River Bank has launched its first bitcoin-backed loans, working with consumer lender LendingUSA to let eligible borrowers take out between $10,000 and $250,000 against their BTC without selling it. The program is the first time Cross River has originated bitcoin-secured loans itself, according to The Block. LendingUSA runs the application platform, and every loan is made by Cross River, a New Jersey state-chartered bank, according to LendingUSA . How the loans work Borrowers can choose a loan-to-value ratio of 30%, 50% or 70%, which sets how much cash they receive against the value of the bitcoin they pledge. LendingUSA defines the ratio as the loan balance divided by the value of the collateral, so a 50% loan against $100,000 of bitcoin would be $50,000. Two repayment options are offered: interest-only or no monthly payments. On an interest-only loan, borrowers make smaller monthly payments that roughly cover interest, with the principal and any remaining interest due at the end of the term. On a no-monthly-payment loan, the full balance plus interest is due at the end. LendingUSA says borrowers can repay early without penalties or fees . Applicants go through a soft credit check, and LendingUSA says approval rests on the crypto being pledged rather than a credit score. The company says funding typically arrives within one to three business days after the collateral is verified. Custody and margin risk A qualified third-party custodian holds the bitcoin for the life of the loan. Once the loan is repaid in full, the collateral is released back to the borrower, according to the company. The terms carry the usual risk of borrowing against a volatile asset. LendingUSA says that if the value of the bitcoin falls, the loan-to-value ratio rises, and borrowers may be asked to add collateral or pay down the debt to avoid liquidation. The company says it will try to notify borrowers first but cannot guarantee it during fast price moves. The timing matters. Bitcoin was trading near $61,000 on Monday morning, so a borrower at the 70% tier would have far less room before a collateral call than one at the 30% tier. Lower ratios leave a bigger cushion but unlock less cash per bitcoin pledged. LendingUSA markets the loans for uses such as debt consolidation, home improvements and large purchases. The company says it has served more than 200,000 borrowers across its lending business, and the crypto product is its first expansion into digital asset-backed loans. business.title: Bitcoin Core Patches Node-Stall Bug Found by Block’s AI Scanner
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Core Patches Node-Stall Bug Found by Block’s AI Scanner Bitcoin Core developers have disclosed and patched a medium-severity bug that let an attacker temporarily freeze a node’s processing of blocks and transactions, a flaw first flagged by an AI scanner built by Block’s Spiral. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-117348, is fixed in Bitcoin Core versions 30.5, 31.3 and 32.1. The 30.5 and 31.3 releases shipped Friday alongside the public advisory, while 32.1 has carried the fix since Oct. 27. Affected versions run from 29.0 through 29.5, 30.0 through 30.4 and 31.0 through 31.2. The 29.x series has reached end of life and will not get a fix, so operators on that branch need to move to a newer release. How the Core bug worked Bitcoin Core keeps “orphan” transactions, whose parent transactions it has not yet seen, and asks peers that announce them for the missing pieces. Since version 29.0, the software builds a list of an orphan’s parents and checks each one against its mempool and filters before deciding what to request. A single inv message can carry up to 50,000 entries, and the software did not skip duplicates. An attacker could send a node an orphan with thousands of missing parents, then send messages repeating that transaction’s ID 50,000 times. “Each such message stalls the node for over a dozen seconds, during which it processes no messages from other peers, including blocks,” the advisory said. Sending more messages could stretch the disruption out. The fix makes the node process each transaction announced in an inv message only once. The advisory describes a temporary denial-of-service problem and does not describe any way to steal bitcoin or permanently damage a node. It also does not say whether the bug was ever exploited. For a business running an affected node, the stalls could still matter. An exchange could be slow to credit deposits, and a miner could keep working on an outdated view of the chain while its node is stuck. An AI-found bug under a faster disclosure policy The advisory credits an automated LLM scan run through Elias Rohrer’s Project Loupe at Spiral, Block’s open-source bitcoin development arm. Bitcoin Core developer Gregory Sanders validated the finding and brought it to the project’s security team. Loupe is a free scanner that runs AI agents over open-source bitcoin code and only reports findings backed by a working test case. Bitcoin Core, BDK, LDK, rust-bitcoin, Cashu, Blockstream Jade, bitcoinj and SRI signed up for its first round of scans. Rohrer said on a recent podcast that Spiral started the project around March and began continuous scanning in May, with Bitcoin Core in the first batch. Loupe reported the issue on July 8. A developer known as Stutxo independently reported it on Aug. 4, the same day Sanders opened a pull request with the fix, which was merged two days later. entertainment.description: For many people, buying property is one of the biggest financial decisions they will ever make. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. It is a challenge Solape Fayemi hopes to address with the launch of Saina Properties , a real estate company now operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Officially unveiled at an event held on 17 November at the Marriott Hotel, Ikeja GRA, Lagos, Saina Properties is built around a simple idea: property ownership should be guided by sound advice, proper verification and professional support, not just the excitement of closing a deal. For Solape, whose experience in the investment industry shaped her understanding of money, risk and wealth creation, the decision to establish the company came from recognising the need for a more considered approach to real estate. “We are not building Saina Properties because the world needs another company selling properties. We are building Saina because we believe there is room for a different kind of real estate experience. One where advice comes before the transaction, where due diligence is not treated as an inconvenience, and where people are encouraged to ask questions, understand their options and make informed decisions,” she said at the launch. That philosophy is reflected in the company’s three core areas of expertise: Advisory & Verification, Sales & Brokerage, and Developments . Rather than focusing solely on connecting buyers to properties, Saina brings together the guidance investors need to assess opportunities, the support required to navigate property transactions, and involvement in real estate development. The company is also building on experience gained before its official launch, having supported more than 25 clients with property opportunities across different markets. An important part of its proposition is the role of professional expertise in protecting property investors. Fayemi’s position raises a familiar question: people consult doctors for medical concerns and lawyers for legal matters, so why do some investors leave significant property decisions in the hands of relatives simply because they are available or familiar with the location? While trust and family relationships matter, they do not automatically translate into the technical knowledge needed to assess a property, verify its documentation or understand its investment potential. These decisions require proper checks, market understanding and accountability. With its operations spanning four markets, Saina Properties aims to support individuals and investors looking to navigate property ownership with greater clarity, whether they are buying, selling or exploring development opportunities. I like organising things, bringing people together, and seeing an idea move forward to get accomplished. So I have known that going to Oxford was never going to be just about getting a master’s degree. Let me explain how I ended up there. entertainment.description: Have you ever spent six hours in an airport waiting for your connecting flight, watching the departure screens, browsing duty-free shops and wondering what the city outside looks like? Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. These are important considerations, but there is another question worth asking: What else can this ticket give me? I am talking about stopovers, not the hurried two-hour connection where you are running between terminals, but an intentional break in your journey that allows you to experience another destination before continuing to the country you originally planned to visit. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. First, Understand What You Are Booking A layover is generally a connection between flights; a stopover is a longer, planned break in your journey. Airlines define these differently, and the distinction matters because some offer special hotel packages, sightseeing tours or complimentary accommodation to qualifying passengers. For example, imagine travelling from Lagos to London through Istanbul. Instead of spending a few hours at Istanbul Airport, you could investigate whether your ticket qualifies for a longer stopover, allowing you to explore Istanbul before continuing to London. entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. (Photo by Aryanna Frank/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images We’re a quarter of the way through the 2027 Willie McCovey Memorial Community Prospect List! Our goal is to rank the top 44 prospects in the San Francisco Giants organization, and we’ve officially hit the 25% mark! Rounding out the first quarter is one of the many new players to the system who is on the list: left-handed pitcher Carson Bolemon, who makes his CPL debut as the No. 11 prospect in the system. The Giants drafted Bolemon with the 29th pick in July’s draft out of Southside Christian School in South Carolina. While he’s a little old for a prep player (he’ll turn 20 in April), he’s extremely experienced, as he not only starred in high school (where he threw a 19-strikeout no-hitter in the state championship game), but was also the ace of the 18-and-under Team USA squad that won the World Cup in 2025. Depending on how you like to view things, it’s either good or bad news that Bolemon was available to the Giants at No. 29, since he entered the season as the consensus top pitcher in the draft. Seen through an optimistic lens, the Giants were able to capitalize on a mildly-down year and get the pre-season top-ranked pitcher … as well as the post-season top-ranked pitcher, Jackson Flora. Seen through a more pessimistic lens, the Giants drafted a player who has already started moving downwards, as he was the ninth pitcher off the board in July, after being projected to be the first pitcher off the board a year ago. Bolemon, who is a well-built 6’4, and who famously didn’t give up a single earned run his junior year, has a fastball that’s been a little inconsistent in terms of velocity, but that has good movement that should allow it to play against righties and lefties alike. He has a very intriguing curveball, while also throwing a changeup and a sweeper, and scouts have raved about his makeup. The Giants were able to draft Bolemon because they acquired the competitive balance-round pick from the Cleveland Guardians in the Patrick Bailey trade, and ultimately those two will forever be linked. That trade will remain something of a “TBD” until we learn how good Bolemon can be, and we’re still many years away from that. Until then, we can look forward to seeing the youngster on the mound in 2027 for his professional debut, as he didn’t pitch (other than in unofficial games) post-draft. It will be interesting to see whether the Giants have Bolemon begin the year in the Arizona Complex League, or if they get him out at the start of the season by sending him to Low-A San Jose. sports.title: BYU has never won a Maui Invitational championship. How can this year’s Cougars change that?
sports.description: BYU players prepare to take the court against Ohio State on Nov. 2, 2026, at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City. | BYU Photo LAHAINA, Hawaii — The Lahaina Civic Center gymnasium is packed with history. Banners hang from its rafters commemorating past Maui Invitational champions, with Duke, North Carolina and Kansas dominating the count. Walls of the arena are dedicated to former Maui standouts and tournament MVPs, such as Kemba Walker, Adam Morrison, Bobby Hurley and Penny Hardaway. Nowhere to be found in the historic gym, however, is a lasting trace of BYU, despite the Cougars having participated in the Maui Invitational there four times before. In fact, as BYU makes its fifth-ever Maui appearance this week, the Cougars are now tied with San Diego State for the second-most times playing in the event without capturing a championship there. Only Memphis has made more trips to Maui (six) without ever hoisting the Wayne Duke trophy, which is presented to the lone unbeaten team after three days of hoops. Additionally, BYU has never produced an invitational MVP, and only one former Cougar — Tyler Haws in 2014 — has landed on the All-Tournament team. Given the current state of both November multi-team events and college basketball as a whole, perhaps 2026 will be the last time BYU graces the Civic Center hardwood in Lahaina and drains shots on the arena’s famous “soft rims.” It’s a shame that one of the sport’s most unique and prestigious early-season traditions is viewed as “on life support” and facing “an uncertain future.” The Protect College Sports Act could easily receive increased support from every political side if it included provisions to save the Maui Invitational — but that’s a thought for another day. If this week truly is the Cougars’ last dance in Maui, it’s their last chance to be crowned champions of the event. And it may be the best such chance they’ve ever had to do so. BYU (No. 25 in KenPom) opens its Maui slate Monday against Washington (No. 88), then will face either Ole Miss (No. 27) or Clemson (No. 75) on Tuesday. Two wins would put the Cougars in Wednesday’s title game, where many fans and pundits anticipate them to meet fellow Big 12 foe Arizona, assuming the Wildcats can survive their bracket of Colorado State, Providence and VCU. Not since 1992 has BYU reached the Maui championship game. The Cougars will likely be favored on both Monday and Tuesday, and in a situation with three games in three days, anything can happen in that third game — even toppling Arizona, if need be. “A lot of it’s going to come down to just toughness,” BYU head coach Kevin Young said of the invitational’s rapid-fire format. “I think our guys possess a lot of that.” BYU’s first time in Maui, 1992, saw the Cougars finish as runners-up, beating No. 9 Oklahoma and then Penny Hardaway-led Memphis before falling to Grant Hill, Bobby Hurley and No. 1 Duke in the championship. sports.title: Syracuse men’s basketball: fans don’t have to pretend all wins are good ones
sports.description: Nov 21, 2026; Syracuse, New York, USA; Syracuse Orange head coach Gerry McNamara reacts during the second half against the Lafayette Leopards at the JMA Wireless Dome. Mandatory Credit: Rich Barnes-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After watching the Syracuse Orange struggle with Cornell on Wednesday, I assumed that Saturday’s game would bring out a focused, energetic squad. That didn’t happen and after having to pull out all the stops to win 84-81 over a Lafayette team that had lost by 36 to Butler and 28 to St. Bonaventure, Gerry McNamara was asked a question about the margin of victory in the wins this week. “I don’t worry. I’ll let other people worry about that nonsense, bullshit, I don’t care. Win a game you know. That’s how I grew up…..I’m not going to worry about margin of victory, all that. I know the next game I play I’m going to coach to win again. So I don’t worry about al the other stuff because at the end of the day you’re still going to have those opponents to play anyway so if you beat them, the margin of victory doesn’t, just win the game you’re playing in front of you. So my focus is on can we continue to get better.” McNamara ended the answer by talking about shooting and offense, but is that the issue? Can we talk about Syracuse’s defense giving up 80+ points to two teams this week? What about the fact that Cornell and Lafayette went 24-54 from 3 in the two games? Unfortunately for anyone who wants to espouse “Just win baby”, it’s not the case in today’s college basketball. Syracuse built their schedule around the NET formula and margin of victory against teams ranked 200th and 303rd in this morning’s KenPom is a factor. Winning 20 or 21 games might not be enough for an invite when the ACC is not off to a strong start. Right now Syracuse sits 81st in KenPom. Last year’s sub-500 team finished the year ranked 87th and the lowest ranked NCAA at-large team was Missouri who was 54th. Yes, it’s early. Yes, you have to win the games, but you cannot pretend that this shouldn’t be a concern….because it is. He went on to talk about not having juice, but why wait until it’s 20+ minutes in the game to make an adjustment to the press? This is still a young staff and they sure don’t seem to have a grasp on what they want this team to be this season. If you’re heading into desperation mode against Lafayette, even with two starters injured, that’s a big warning sign. This was a November game that almost turned into a unfathomable loss and it wasn’t the time to lecture anyone about playing to win the game. I’m sensititve to the fact that Gerry’s dealing with a lot right now- on and off the court. I’m worried that the pressure he’s putting on himself to get this program back is too much, but you can’t get this agitated over a legitimate question. He didn’t mention ISIS , but there were a lot of Shafer vibes coming out of this one….let’s hope the Albany post-game talk stays out of “cutting people’s heads off” talk.

sports.description: Freeman has 11 tries in 31 matches for England [Getty Images] England wing Tommy Freeman is in contention for Saturday's Nations Championship play-off meeting with New Zealand. The 25-year-old has been a key part of England's backline this year, starting nine Tests in a row for before being rotated out of the side for their comprehensive win over Japan on 14 November. He was due to return for the 37-12 win over the All Blacks on Saturday, but a thigh issue forced his withdrawal in the hours before kick-off. Harlequins' Cadan Murley was called into the side to replace Freeman and impressed in an emphatic England performance. Head coach Steve Borthwick has bolstered his back-three options, which also include Gloucester's Will Joseph, by calling up Saracens' 20-year-old Noah Caluori. Caluori, who finished as joint-top try scorer in last year's Prem alongside Freeman, crossed on his England debut against Fiji in July and was a late replacement in the win over Argentina a week later. He also scored two tries in a England A's win over an Argentine equivalent earlier this month. Fly-half Fin Smith, who came off 55 minutes into the win over the All Blacks with cramp, is also in a 37-strong squad who have gathered at England's training base to prepare for Saturday's third-place play-off. England finished a point short of France in the northern hemisphere standings of the new format, missing out on a place in Sunday's Nations Championship final against South Africa. The result of England and New Zealand's meeting, along with the weekend's other five matches at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium, will contribute to a Ryder Cup-style points race for the inaugural hemisphere shield. sports.description: James Gallagher bidding farewell to mixed martial arts at age 30 on Sunday flooded my mind with memories of him as a teenage prodigy, bustling Bellator Dublin shows and a feeling that despite never realizing the glory he thought he would, his career is one of the most successful in Irish MMA history. A highlight reel of Ricky Bandejas’ 2018 upset of Gallagher will flicker through a lot of people’s minds when they think of “The Strabanimal.” There was a collective euphoria across social media back then seeing the 21-year-old eat a side kick before getting pounded out, just a few minutes after being all up in Bandejas’s face. It’s the quintessential “chat s***, get banged” scenario playing out at a live sporting event. In fact, it’s such a classic of the genre, you’ll likely still see it pop up on your feed today, nearly a decade later. To simmer Gallagher’s career down to that one brutal defeat would be massively underselling the impact he had on the sport in his home country, though. As a teenager, Gallagher was like a mythological creature. Fighting grown men at age 13, it wasn’t until he was introduced to SBG head coach John Kavanagh that his dream began to take shape. His jiu-jitsu ability was the first thing most people heard about him. Experienced black belts would wax lyrical about his potential after his move to Dublin. Then, after blitzing through all the youth competitions, he began showing up at adult events and proving it wasn’t just hot air. James Gallagher and coach John Kavanaugh were a formidable duo early in Gallagher's MMA run. ASSOCIATED PRESS There was a buzz across the mats when Gallagher was competing. sports.title: Nationals reliever Erik Tolman given the Tony Conigliaro award for his inspirational rise
sports.description: WASHINGTON, DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA - SEPTEMBER 27, 2026: Erik Tolman #73 of the Washington Nationals pitches during the ninth inning of a game against the New York Mets at Nationals Park on September 27, 2026 in Washington, District of Columbia. The Nationals beat the Mets, 6-4. (Photo by Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Erik Tolman’s debut and success in the big leagues was one of the best stories in baseball during the 2026 season. The Nats left handed reliever had to overcome so many obstacles to get on to an MLB mound, but he did it. Today, Tolman was awarded with the Tony Conigliaro Award, which is given to a big leaguer who has overcome adversity. honoring erik 🙌 the Tony Conigliaro Award award recognizes a major leaguer who has overcome adversity through the attributes of spirit, determination, and courage. pic.twitter.com/uHrAbbMGzM — Washington Nationals (@Nationals) November 23, 2026 Conigliaro was a Red Sox player in the late 1960’s who was on the road to superstardom before getting hit in the face with a ball. That hit by pitch caused major damage, including some vision loss. Despite that, Conigliaro came back after missing a season. He put up quality numbers in 1969 and 1970, before the vision problems became so bad, he could not play anymore. The award has been handed out since 1990, and is usually given out to players who dealt with serious injuries or other health issues. Wilson Ramos is the only other National to win the award. He won it in 2014 due to coming back from injuries and a kidnapping. Tolman now joins him as a Nat to win the award. Tolman’s story is a ridiculous tale of perseverance. He had to undergo Tommy John twice in a short period of time after being drafted. That is bad enough, but these days that is not unheard of. However, in his return, Tolman tore up every ligament in his knee and more after his foot got stuck jumping over the foul line. This clip from Just Baseball does a good job explaining everything. MLB’s Story of the YEAR Erik Tolman of the Nationals comeback story is incredible pic.twitter.com/ee8hI3rVrZ — Just Baseball (@JustBB_Media) November 6, 2026 The biggest long term health problem from that injury was foot drop. Tolman is unable to move his foot side to side due to nerve damage. During that injury, his peroneal nerve was cut. So when Tolman is on the mound, he has to wear an ankle brace for stabilization. technology.title: Critical Cisco remote code execution bug under attack
technology.description: Attackers are currently exploiting a critical vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-76466 in Cisco Expressway that allows them to remotely execute commands as root without any authentication, according to warnings from the US government and security researchers. CVE-2026-76466 , which carries a 9.8 CVSS rating, affects Cisco Expressway-C and Cisco Expressway-E gateways configured in clusters, both virtual and physical appliances running vulnerable software. These provide firewall traversal, VPN-less remote access, and call routing for remote users connecting to voice, video, and messaging collaboration services. The bug involves hard-coded authentication credentials and insufficient certificate validation in clustered Expressway deployments. “An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands,” Cisco said in October, when it disclosed the bug and issued a software update that fixed the flaw. “A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root on the underlying operating system of an affected device.” At the time, the networking vendor said it wasn’t aware of any abuse of the vulnerability. That all changed late last week, however, when Russian security firm F6 said it was investigating “the first observed case” of miscreants exploiting CVE-2026-76466, shortly after a public proof-of-concept exploit became available. “The attackers initially compromised two Cisco Expressway internet-facing devices,” F6’s Cyber Defense Center said on Thursday. “Through one of them, they gained access to two additional cluster nodes located on the organization’s internal network. After obtaining root access, the attackers began preparing tooling for further lateral movement across the infrastructure.” Specifically, the criminals prepared custom Python code to scan the victim’s network and identify files and folders shared over the Server Message Block (SMB) protocol. The scripts were also designed to interact with SQL Server and WinRM, and search GitLab repositories for credentials and other sensitive information. The Python scripts used in the attack indicated that the operator used an AI assistant, according to F6. The security shop also noted that one of the key indicators of compromise is a nodeup “wombat@127.0.0.1” entry in the Erlang system log (erlang.log) on affected Cisco Expressway devices. A day later, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added CVE-2026-76466 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, and told federal agencies to patch by Monday. Cisco updated its advisory on Monday to acknowledge CISA’s addition, while noting that it has no direct evidence of active exploitation. The Register reached out to the networking and security vendor for additional details about the scope of the attacks, but did not receive any response. We will update this story as we learn more. ®

technology.title: Bulgaria evicts cyber snoops who lurked inside government networks for 5 years
technology.description: The Ancient Thracian heartland of Bulgaria says it has shut down a cyberespionage operation that gave intruders access to government networks for five years – the longest-running known campaign against its administration. Bulgaria's Ministry of Innovation and Digital Transformation said the unauthorized and officially unattributed attackers first gained access to infrastructure used by government institutions to exchange information in 2021. It explained that the intrusion went unnoticed for so long because "the previous means of protection did not work as a single, integrated system," and that without a new, recently installed product, it may have gone undetected for much longer. "The incident was discovered thanks to the new national cybersecurity system, which for the first time provides a single picture of what is happening in state networks," the ministry added. "Without it, this activity would most likely have remained hidden for an indefinite period of time." Bulgaria acknowledged that "sensitive information related to the work of the state" was accessed, but did not specify the scale of the compromise. Innovation and Digital Transformation Minister Ivan Vasilev said attackers had downloaded more than 130 GB of data over five years. He also put the volume at 62 million pages. The Register contacted the Bulgarian government for confirmation of these numbers. The ministry said that it has not yet found any evidence that citizens' personal data was compromised, and that the affected infrastructure "will be under increased surveillance for 90 days" in case the attackers try to regain access. Vasilev said multiple international hacking groups had accessed government systems since 2021. He did not specify the names of these groups, however, nor did he name any specific countries that may have been involved. In a follow-up interview with bTV , Vasilev blamed political instability and frequent changes of ministerial leadership for leaving government systems inadequately protected. A representative of the Progressive Bulgaria party, which back in May won Bulgaria's eighth general election in five years, Vasilev said the "constant change of leadership" means "important things for the state do not actually happen." Vasilev said the intrusion was discovered over the summer as the national cybersecurity system was upgraded, and that teams had spent the past three to four months removing the attackers. ®

technology.title: Microsoft mega outage: Report reveals testing gaps and emails that never arrived
technology.description: Some emails never reached their recipients during November's Microsoft 365 outage, the company has confirmed in a final report that also exposes gaps in its testing and recovery procedures. The post-incident report details how a Windows defect brought down Exchange Online and disrupted features across other Microsoft 365 services. For affected users, the cloud became someone else's unavailable computer. A preliminary report had already blamed a July code change, combined with a failover and reduced capacity. The final report confirms those findings and sets out Microsoft's plans to improve change auditing and recovery procedures, and add spare capacity. The defect affected Microsoft's gateway server configuration, not standard Windows deployments. The epic outage (named the "Microsoft long weekend" by some wags) kicked off on November 12 and wasn't fully resolved until November 14. Microsoft extended its delivery retry window to 48 hours, but some delayed messages destined for consumer mailboxes inactive for more than 30 days still expired, generating non-delivery reports. The company said all queued enterprise messages were eventually delivered, with none found permanently lost. The report is grim, particularly in how the failure ramped up as US users came online to find gateway servers toppling over. At the worst point, more than 80 percent of North American gateway servers were unresponsive. The problem proved elusive, and it took Microsoft some time to identify the change and deploy a fix. Microsoft has had a week to ponder what it did and did not do, and the report has some next steps to avoid a repeat of November's events. Some are obvious, and some are a little surprising. Working to reduce the blast radius of failures is an obvious one, and actions include partitioning and isolation to ensure failures can be contained before taking down traffic globally. Recovery procedures also need improvement, along with communication and capacity to ensure there is sufficient headroom. Microsoft's load tests used older, lower-core-count hardware, making them less likely to expose a defect that worsened on newer machines. The company now plans to test newer hardware with more realistic traffic and peak loads, and broaden its failover testing. Microsoft also plans to improve diagnostics and change auditing so engineers can identify troublesome Windows changes faster. July's defect had been running worldwide for more than three months before it brought the gateways down. ®

technology.title: British retailer Next downplays data breach at tech supplier
technology.description: British retailer Next has become the latest high street name to find itself caught up in a cyberattack, although it insists the data accessed by hackers is "benign" and its customers have nothing to worry about. The clothing and homeware giant told investors on Monday that a third-party supplier had suffered a security breach, allowing an unauthorized party to access information relating to Next. The retailer says its own systems remain untouched and that, so far, there's no evidence that customer personal data has fallen into the wrong hands. "We have been informed that one of our third-party online suppliers has experienced a cyber incident which has resulted in unauthorized access to certain benign data relating to NEXT," the company said in its statement, which it shared with The Register . "We took immediate steps to investigate the nature and scope of the incident with the supplier." The breached supplier provides technology services to Next, and the "benign" information accessed is understood to be low-level data. Sensitive customer details, including addresses, passwords, and banking information, are believed to be unaffected. Next hasn't identified the supplier, explained exactly what the hackers managed to get their hands on, or revealed how much information was accessed, and declined to say when asked by The Register . However, the retailer has seemingly decided that the stolen data won’t be of much use to the criminals responsible. "Our investigations are ongoing; however, current evidence indicates that no customer personal data has been compromised," Next said. "The information affected is limited in nature and, based on our current assessment, cannot be used to facilitate fraud against our customers or NEXT." Next also stressed that its own IT infrastructure had escaped unscathed, saying it was "confident that NEXT’s own systems have not been compromised and that this remains an incident affecting the supplier's environment." Despite repeatedly describing the compromised information as harmless, Next says it is treating the incident "with the utmost seriousness" and is working with the affected supplier, law enforcement, and relevant regulators. The incident comes just weeks after fellow British fashion retailer Asos suffered a breach of its own , with hackers gaining access to customer information through third-party platforms. That attack, which came to light on October 6 when customers received an unauthorized push notification through the Asos app announcing that the company had been hacked, was traced to a social engineering scam. An attacker impersonated a trusted contact to trick an Asos employee into handing over login credentials, which were then used to access external platforms. Darryl covers aviation and the FAA, and earlier this month, when the US suffered a sudden nationwide ground stop on air travel, Darryl was all over the story. (Image credit: ESA/DLR/FU Berlin) Researchers have spotted an ancient, "dead" Martian volcano from orbit around the Red Planet. What is it? The European Space Agency's Mars Express spacecraft, which has been orbiting and studying the planet since it arrived in 2003, recently captured incredible new imagery of the volcano Tharsis Tholus. This snapshot was captured by the spacecraft's High Resolution Stereo Camera. Even as old and worn as it is, the Martian volcano stands at around 4.97 miles (8 kilometers) tall which is comparable to some of the highest peaks in the Himalayan mountains. Despite its impressive height, it's still only about a medium-sized volcano for Mars, which is home much more impressively-sized volcanoes. For example, the planet's largest volcano Olympus Mons measures in at roughly 13.2 miles high (21.3 kilometers). Tharsis Tholus, a volcano on the surface of Mars, as seen by ESA's Mars Express orbiter. (Image credit: ESA/DLR/FU Berlin) Why is it incredible? While Tharsis Tholus might not be the tallest volcano on Mars, it is incredibly steep. It is steeper than Mauna Kea in Hawaii on Earth. To fully showcase the volcano's structure and topography in 3D, researchers actually exaggerated the vertical scale in this image, ESA reported . In addition to being steep and fairly tall, the volcano also has an interesting history. You can see that it is speckled with what look like small holes which are actually craters created by impacts from objects like asteroids. The volcano's current, unique shape is a combined effort by these impacts, environmental factors causing erosion and warping and ancient lava flows that left behind built-up material. The observations by Mars Express also reveals cracks and other imperfections in the volcano. All of these details might seem like superficial bits of detail, however every small crater, every lumpy cliffside and every worn down surface hides information about the planet's past. By studying features like volcanoes on Mars, researchers can piece together what the planet may have looked like in its ancient past. How active was this volcano? How did it interact with the landscape around it? Observations like this can hold the answers.

After a tortuous fortnight of negotiations, COP31 ended in disarray late on 22 November after countries including the UK and the EU refused to agree to a political accord that failed to mention fossil fuels. Read more Can everyone live a ‘good life’ without destroying the planet? The Antalya pact would have seen countries officially recognise that the world is on course to exceed 1.5°C degrees of warming and promise to limit the scale of the overshoot as far as possible. It also would have committed nations to increasing the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35 per cent globally by 2035, a key target for climate campaigners who see electrification as the route away from fossil-fuel dependency. Advertisement But the draft agreement proved unacceptable to many countries, including the UK, the EU and some small island nations, after all mentions of fossil fuels were omitted at the behest of fossil fuel-dependent nations such as Saudi Arabia and Russia. Failing to mention fossil fuels explicitly in the text would have marked a backwards step for the climate process, the EU argued. At COP28 in Dubai three years ago, nations agreed to “transition away from fossil fuels” , but since then, attempts to strengthen the language or clarify how this transition will take place have been blocked by petrostates. Alden Meyer at the climate think tank E3G says the talks were subjected to a “brutish” strategy from fossil fuel-exporting states to “systematically block” any reference to the COP28 deal. “They clearly have buyer’s remorse about that agreement. science.title: What did the Soviet Union's final deep space probe actually see on Mars?

Micah Hanks is a science reporter and podcaster focusing on space and astronomy, and Editor at TheDebrief.org. Follow him on X @MicahHanks.

On July 12, 1988, Phobos 2 — one of the Soviet Union's final major planetary exploration probes — was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome aboard a Proton rocket. The spacecraft's mission included the study of Mars and the Martian moon Phobos, with a planned close approach and deployment of landing probes, and over the next several months, the spacecraft successfully captured more than three dozen images of Phobos during its time in service. However, early in the following year, the spacecraft's mission abruptly ended after the Phobos 2 ground team mysteriously lost contact with the spacecraft. Adding to the mystery were objects in some of the final photographs dispatched by the doomed spacecraft, which seemed to show an elongated shadow beneath the probe — a strange twist in one of the Soviet Union's final space missions, and one that soon gave rise to conspiracy theories about what the fate of Phobos 2 might have been. So what caused the odd-looking appearance of the shadow in the final images captured by Phobos 2, and what was the real reason behind the spacecraft's sudden failure? Last of the Soviet space explorers Originally, the Soviet Union had planned for Phobos 2 to reach the Red Planet by late January 1989, after which the spacecraft would begin collecting data about the Martian environment leading up to its initial contact with Mars' largest moon in early June. The stakes were almost immediately raised as Phobos 2 arrived in orbit around Mars on Jan. 30, 1989 , when one of the probe's three onboard flight system processors was found to have gone offline, with another already experiencing technical issues. science.title: Astronomers just discovered a rare triple star system 28 light-years away, and they have ‘no clean explanation for how it got here’
science.description: A triple system containing a dim red dwarf star and not one but two white dwarfs has been fortuitously discovered just 28 light-years away from our solar system. "We were actually looking for planets ," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement . "Instead, we found something much more surprising." So surprising that there are no similar systems within at least 100 light-years . Furthermore, the configuration of the system seems impossible. "This system should not exist," added Montreal's Patrick Dufour. "We have no clean explanation for how it got here." This triple system has been called Welopō'ai, which is a portmanteau of two Hawaiian words that means a 'path of family traits', and to understand the mystery behind it requires astronomers to figure out the history of the three objects. A white dwarf is what remains when a star of similar mass to our sun reaches the end of its life. As it begins to run low on hydrogen for nuclear fusion reactions in its core, the star's energy generation begins to falter and its interior starts to contract under gravity . This has the effect of raising the temperature throughout the star, causing an outer shell of hydrogen to ignite its own fusion reactions. The star promptly bloats to become a red giant tens or even hundreds of millions of kilometers across. Soon enough the star ceases fusion reactions completely. The star's outer layers are shed and they expand out into space, while its core contracts to become an inert white dwarf with a diameter similar to Earth but with a mass generally between half and two-thirds of a solar mass . Therefore, the Welopō'ai system was once a triple system with two sun-like stars plus the red dwarf. Now the two sun-like stars have undergone this stage of star death while their companion red dwarf continues to linger, since its low mass bequeaths it a longer life because it does not use up its core hydrogen as quickly. One of the white dwarfs orbits the red dwarf at a distance of 129.3 astronomical units (19.3 billion kilometers or 12 billion miles) and takes about 1,000 years to complete one orbit. This white dwarf and the red dwarf were previously known, and Artigau's team had been using the SPectropolarimètre InfraROUge (SPIRou) instrument on the Canada–France–Hawaii Telescope atop Mauna Kea to search for planets orbiting the red dwarf when they noticed something highly unusual. NASA Earth Observatory/Lauren Dauphin More than 60 years ago, scientists at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center aimed a laser skyward and fired a pulse of light at an orbiting satellite equipped with special reflectors. By measuring the time it took for the light to return, they demonstrated a new, more precise method for tracking satellites. Since then, satellite laser ranging (SLR) has grown more precise and more widely used. The technique now underpins many aspects of Earth observation, such as validating satellite orbits and mapping subtle changes to Earth’s surface. Pioneered at the Goddard Optical Research Facility—now the Goddard Geophysical and Astronomical Observatory —laser ranging is performed at more than 40 stations worldwide. In 2026, the next generation of SLR, developed by NASA scientists and tested at Goddard, began to come online. On October 12, a faster, even more precise SLR system officially debuted at the Ny-Ålesund Geodetic Observatory in Svalbard, Norway, operated by the Norwegian Mapping Authority, a NASA partner. The observatory’s remote location in the Arctic archipelago is shown in this image, acquired with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 in July 2026. It is the first NASA next-generation SLR system in operation and the northernmost SLR facility on Earth. While the systems developed decades ago have been “workhorses” of the global laser tracking network, their age and the growing number of satellites have necessitated updates, said Stephen Merkowitz, project manager for NASA’s Space Geodesy Project . “We wanted newer systems that could track more objects, and track them more accurately and precisely,” he said. The Space Geodesy Satellite Laser Ranging system fires at the Ny-Ålesund Geodetic Observatory in Svalbard, Norway, against a backdrop of aurora borealis on October 7, 2026. NASA/Julie Horvath (KBR) Years of development, testing, and careful calibration produced the Space Geodesy Satellite Laser Ranging system now running at Ny-Ålesund. Among its features are lasers that can fire pulses thousands of times per second, up from tens of times per second, and sensors that can detect single photons, meaning that less light needs to be reflected back from a satellite. science.title: Ariane 6 rocket launching 36 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit on Nov. 24 after delay: Watch it live
science.description: null Amazon's first satellite launch since a rocket failure doomed 40 of its spacecraft is set for Tuesday morning (Nov. 24), and you can watch the action live. An Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation is scheduled to lift off from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana, on Tuesday (Nov. 23), during a 29-minute window that opens at 5:45 a.m. EST (1045 GMT; 7:45 a.m. local time in Kourou). You can watch it live here at Space.com courtesy of Arianespace, the French company that operates the Ariane 6. The launch was originally supposed to take place on Monday (Nov. 23), but that attempt was scrubbed due to a technical issue affecting the rocket's ground support systems, according to Arianespace . Amazon Leo, so named because it will operate in low Earth orbit , will compete with SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 operational spacecraft. Amazon's network will eventually have more than 3,200 satellites, but just 400 or so have reached orbit to date. Another 40 were supposed to be delivered on Nov. 15, but they were lost after their rocket ride, a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan Centaur , suffered a problem shortly after launch. Ariane 6 and Vulcan Centaur aren't the only rockets Amazon is depending on to build its broadband constellation. Jeff Bezos' company has also booked rides on ULA's Atlas V rocket, Blue Origin's New Glenn and SpaceX's Falcon 9 . Vulcan will be grounded for a while as ULA investigates the Nov. 15 failure and works to fix whatever caused it. And New Glenn hasn't flown since April, when the rocket failed to deliver AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite to the proper orbit. New Glenn's return to flight was further complicated on May 28, when the rocket exploded during a routine prelaunch test. The Ariane 6, the successor to Arianespace's Ariane 5 heavy lifter, debuted in July 2024 and has nine launches under its belt to date. All of them have been successful except that maiden mission, which was a partial failure. The upcoming mission will be the fourth Amazon Leo flight for the Ariane 6, following launches in February, April and June of this year.
